title: Adjusted warmth by rain-deficit intervals crossed zero for autumn timing in two northern US camera samples in 2008-2023
abstract: We tested whether low summer rain makes the link between summer warmth and autumn canopy timing more negative. Four eastern US region and period tests were planned. Two northern models used 129 camera-years in 2008-2015 and 2016-2023. Their interaction estimates were +1.27 and -2.93 days per degree C per local rain standard deviation. Both four-test adjusted intervals included zero. Year-sign tests gave p = 0.391 and 0.156. The two southern samples had only five and seven usable cameras, below the planned minimum of eight, and were not fit. Most model checks kept a negative later northern estimate but did not establish a repeated result. Changing the spatial groups and comparing current with next-year weather gave isolated adjusted intervals below zero in later North. These are associations in optical canopy timing, not causal climate effects or direct measures of leaf senescence. Few years, changing camera membership, selected single-cycle seasons and remaining observation bias limit inference. Pollution and daily extremes were not tested. The package includes code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, figures, reusable NOAA weather statistics and independent numerical checks. PhenoCam source records stay external.

display.caption: Both northern primary interaction intervals include zero after correction for four planned tests. The southern samples do not meet the planned camera minimum. Calendar slots include years before camera installation and after its last image; they are not attempted surveys. Thick lines show ordinary 95 percent intervals. Thin lines show four-test intervals.

Checks in the two northern periods do not establish a repeated interaction. The later northern estimate remains negative, but most four-test intervals include zero. A larger spatial block and the current-minus-next-year contrast give isolated intervals below zero. These checks reuse the records and are not independent replications.

citations.reason: Frozen PhenoCam V3 camera archives supply observed image coverage and estimated optical transition dates.
Prior North American canopy timing models motivate the weather question. Some camera records can overlap; this is not independent validation of the earlier study.
Canopy greenness loss must be kept separate from physiological leaf senescence.
